blockers.quote: Inside it, one room, one window, one clock: a room where time runs at the old speed, a day for a day
blockers.why: Fails “No new power rule after the halfway point” and check #16: the mechanism that enables the climax first appears after 80% of the runtime.
blockers.fix: Plant it during line 45’s first-year montage: “You pass one room where the wall clock moves at outside speed. A minute for a minute. Useless, when you have a year.” Withhold the queue until the climax.

blockers.quote: Night two you learn to cook. Night three you read every book in the inside town's library. Night four, a language. Night five, another.
blockers.why: Fails check #6, Every use has a gap: four uses deliver exactly the expected benefit before the montage’s later door-code turn.
blockers.fix: Replace with: “Night two, you learn to cook—and make the breakfast she told you yesterday she hates. Night three, every book inside—and not the note she left outside. Night four, one language. Night five, another. When she asks how you slept, the word you need is in neither.”

blockers.quote: Then the stake, 0:38: "She just stayed at one speed. And you've got work in the morning."
blockers.why: Fails check #3: the outline explicitly delays the second hook and personal loss until after 0:30.
blockers.fix: Move the stake immediately after the title question, around 0:20: “She stays at one speed. Every year you gain in there pushes last night with her a year farther away.”

suggestions.quote: If she plugs in tonight, she doesn't arrive beside you. She arrives a newcomer in year forty-one of your life in there
suggestions.fix: Owner suggestion: resolve the contradiction with line 48’s shared town. Make joining you threaten to erase her outside life too, so refusing her protects the person she is rather than treating “newcomer” as an insurmountable barrier.

suggestions.quote: lose the forty years of friends who are more of your life than she is
suggestions.fix: Give the inside side of the dilemma a face: bring back the piano teacher during the final goodbye and let that established person ask you to stay.

suggestions.quote: And if you'd have done the same, hit like and subscribe.
suggestions.fix: Cut the spoken like-and-subscribe sentence; keep those requests as silent end-card tags so the closing choice remains the final address.

keep.quote: They're queueing for a room that runs at her speed. You've got one. It's upstairs. It's free.
Tomorrow someone will say 'tell me tomorrow'. Hear how far away that is.
